drivingQuestion: How can the mishna permit repairs when hammering was banned on Chol HaMoed?
outcomeNote: Contradiction raised; resolutions follow in the next unit

segments.he: הַצִּיר וְהַצִּינּוֹר וְהַקּוֹרָה וְהַמַּנְעוּל וְהַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ — מְתַקְּנָן בַּמּוֹעֵד. וּרְמִינְהִי: עַד יָמָיו הָיָה פַּטִּישׁ מַכֶּה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם כּוּ׳. עַד יָמָיו — אִין, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — לָא!
segments.en: It was taught in the mishna: With regard to «the hinge» of a door, «and the cylinder» of the hinge, «and the» cross «beam» that holds the door, «and a lock and a key that broke, one may fix them on» the intermediate days of «a Festival.» The Gemara «raises a contradiction» to this from a different mishna (Ma’aser Sheni 5:15): «Until the days» of Yoḥanan the High Priest, workmen’s «hammers would beat in Jerusalem» on the intermediate days of a Festival. One can deduce from this mishna that «until his days, yes,» the workmen’s hammers would beat, «but from then on, no,» because Yoḥanan the High Priest banned such work. This seems to contradict the mishna here that permits fixing certain items on the intermediate days of the Festival.
